brief.intro: New to this project type? A process / oil & gas facility (a gas plant, oil processing facility, tank farm or compressor station) is a plant whose real product is moving and treating hydrocarbons safely. The building work is minor — the plant is really thousands of metres of process pipe connecting vessels, pumps and compressors, tanks and columns, all wrapped in instrumentation and safety systems. Your schedule is driven by three things: fabricating and erecting the process piping, delivering and setting the rotating equipment (pumps, compressors), and delivering the static equipment (vessels, tanks, columns). Commissioning is organised by system and subsystem — mechanical completion, then loop checks, then start-up — not by area or floor, and nothing touches hydrocarbon until purge, leak test and dry-out are proven.

scope.desc: Underground process/firewater/drainage networks, equipment foundations and anchor bolts, pipe-rack and sleeper foundations.

scope.desc: Pipe racks, pipe bridges and equipment support steel.

scope.desc: Vessels, columns and tanks — procured, set on foundations and aligned.

scope.desc: Pumps and compressors — set, aligned, coupled and run-in.

scope.desc: Spool fabrication, field erection, welding/NDT, flushing and hydrotest.

scope.name: Electrical & hazardous-area works
scope.desc: MV/LV power, Ex-rated equipment, earthing and cabling for classified areas.

scope.name: Instrumentation & control
scope.desc: Field instruments, DCS/PLC and the Safety Instrumented System (SIS/ESD).

scope.name: Fire, gas & firewater
scope.desc: Firewater ring main, deluge/sprinkler systems and fire & gas detection.

scope.name: Pre-commissioning & commissioning
scope.desc: Mechanical completion by system, purge/leak test/dry-out, and start-up.

must_get_right: Spool fabrication, rotating equipment and static equipment (vessels/tanks) are the true long-lead, critical items — track and expedite them from day one.
Commissioning is organised by system, not by area — build the system breakdown (from the P&IDs) early so mechanical completion can be tracked system by system.
Protect the pre-commissioning sequence — purge, leak test, dry-out — before hydrocarbon is introduced; rework at this stage is expensive and unsafe.
Hazardous-area electrical and the firewater/deluge system gate start-up — never let their completion slip behind the piping and equipment.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structural steel run a 6-day week; piping and rotating-equipment erection move to two shifts at peak to protect the critical path; pre-commissioning and commissioning run a 7-day calendar. A weather allowance is embedded in the civil calendar.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs long-lead procurement (vessels, compressors, tanks) → equipment foundations → static/rotating equipment set → process piping fabrication and erection → hydrotest → electrical & instrumentation → pre-commissioning (purge/leak test/dry-out) → SIS/ESD proving → start-up. The structure and site civil works are not on the critical path once foundations and pipe racks are complete.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design and hazardous-area classification are frozen; permits and authority approvals are obtained per phase gate; a single mobilisation; and, where the facility ties into an existing operating plant, tie-in/shutdown windows are agreed and held by the operator in advance. Any change to these invalidates the baseline dates.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy lifts (vessels, compressors, columns) require crane windows and clear laydown/hardstand; hazardous-area work needs a hot-work/cold-work permit system; skilled coded welders and NDT technicians are a resource constraint on the piping fabrication front; brownfield tie-ins depend on operator-controlled shutdown windows.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: long-lead slippage on rotating and static equipment, hydrotest rework, tie-in/shutdown window slip on brownfield sites, and re-test loops on SIS/ESD proving. Schedule contingency is held immediately before pre-commissioning and before start-up rather than spread thinly across activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
